Street images: Changsha, Baidu street view (© Baidu). Scale from Li, Qin & Long (2024), Buildings 14, 3901, doi:10.3390/buildings14123901.

config.description: Method replication: the images are new Baidu street views of central Changsha, turned towards the buildings, not the paper's stimuli. Participants rate each street view on the ten items of the architectural color perception scale (character, vitality, security, cleanliness, belonging, affinity, influence, hue, complexity, harmony), each on a five-point scale between two words (for example Fuzzy–Unique, Bored–Lively; 'Inconsistent–Consistent' means how well the statement matches what you feel), for a total of up to 50 points per image, as in Li, Qin & Long (2024, Buildings). Differences from the original study: (1) the paper picked 60 street views where building colors were clearly visible and had each rated by 3 people; here each participant rates 10 random views; (2) the paper asked for good color vision and recorded architecture training, kept here as questions.

paper.title: Urban Architectural Color Evaluation: A Cognitive Framework Combining Machine Learning and Human Perception
